## TCAD-Aware SPICE Model Extraction with Utmost IV: From Manufacturing to Surrogate Circuit Modeling


### **Abstract**


Accurate compact models are essential for translating device behavior into trustworthy circuit simulation, but extracting a high-quality model card can require substantial expertise, repeated optimization, and extensive manual intervention. In this webinar, we will introduce a new Utmost IV model-extraction flow designed to make this process faster, more efficient, and easier to manage. At the center of the flow is an improved optimizer that significantly reduces the level of user intervention required to extract a model card from device-characteristic data. Attendees will see how Utmost IV supports the progression from device data through parameter extraction, optimization, model validation, and compact SPICE model generation. The webinar will also highlight the role of Utmost IV within Silvaco’s broader simulation environment, connecting device characterization and compact modeling with downstream circuit simulation. Through practical examples, we will demonstrate how the streamlined workflow can help modeling engineers reduce repetitive setup and optimization effort while maintaining control over extraction objectives and results. We will also show how Utmost IV can be incorporated into Silvaco FTCO™ workflows.


**What You Will Learn**


- How the new Utmost IV flow streamlines compact-model extraction from device-characteristic data
- How the improved optimizer reduces manual intervention when extracting model cards
- How to progress from parameter extraction and optimization to model validation and compact SPICE model generation


## Presenter


**Sean Kelly**
**Engineering Manager, Silvaco**


Sean Kelly is the engineering manager for the Utmost IV device characterization and SPICE modeling tools. He has over 35 years experience in process and device design, device characterization, SPICE modeling and EDA software development.


### WHO SHOULD ATTEND:


Compact-modeling engineers, device engineers, characterization engineers, TCAD engineers, PDK and model-library development engineers, and engineering management.
